==> README.md <==
identity/completeness checks, prerequisite-only validation and analysis.
Actual execution requires fresh compatible prerequisites and an explicit
`--execute-study` latch **after separate authorization**. No resume/overwrite.
Analysis supports both recorded matrix parts; incomplete studies cannot produce
paired/cross-input comparisons, and prepared diagnostics never replace production
host-call timing. This is tooling support, not a completed comparison study.

The [safety repair](docs/CPU_GPU_SAFETY_REPAIR_v1.md) adds independent frozen-source
anchor enforcement and a reviewed, fail-closed non-timing test selector.
`python3 -B scripts/non_timing_tests.py --build-dir build/EXISTING_RELEASE` only
prints discovery/selection; it never executes tests. The prerequisite-only
validator now uses that selection and marks its result correctness-only,
`study_eligible=false`. It cannot satisfy the unchanged frozen full-study gate.
No fresh prerequisite run or study was performed by this repair.

The subsequent [CTest build guard](docs/CTEST_BUILD_GUARD_v1.md) validates reviewed
source and generated configuration **before discovery**, including retained JSON.
Hooks, includes, nested registries and unreviewed commands fail closed; metadata
is rechecked before execution. Only inert Python fixtures validated this repair.
No real discovery or selected CTest suite ran. Independent review is next;
study launch remains **NO-GO**.

The follow-up [path-identity repair](results/raw/ctest_path_repair_20261010T234224414430Z/FINAL_AUDIT.md)
pins discovery and downstream selection to the guard's exact absolute build path,
including relative caller arguments and differing callback working directories.
All47 focused inert regressions pass; no CTest, build, prerequisite, resource or
GPU command ran. The approved19 CPU selection and supported layouts are unchanged.
This repair still requires separate independent review; study launch remains NO-GO.

==> docs/AUDIT.md <==
[inert rejection proof](../results/raw/ctest_hook_repair_20261010T223851377458Z/REJECTION_PROOF.json),
[guard contract](CTEST_BUILD_GUARD_v1.md).

Final focused Python validation passes 28 new guard methods and 11 existing
selector methods (39/39, no skips). Real subprocess launch was blocked in the
tests; fake discovery/execution callbacks returned literal fixture data. The
previous review's exact inert hook fixture is rejected with zero callback calls.
The first 26-method run had one error from rejecting a normal P4Command Dart key;
its log and source snapshot remain retained. Static review also corrected the
CUDA backtrace stack policy using retained generated metadata, then retested it.
An initial policy-derivation assertion exposed the existing python3 symlink;
canonical path comparison fixed it without weakening argument matching. A
documentation patch context mismatch made no changes and was corrected.

Direct before/after checks verify all 11,448 prior result files (11,345 historical,
46 earlier repair and 57 independent-review files), 26 protected anchors, four
frozen assets including the pinned freeze, 80 production/header/dependency files
and 21 existing build-metadata files. No differences occurred in those sets.
The separate final integrity manifest records new evidence counts and intended
source/document changes. The selector source policy was explicitly renewed;
frozen protocol and production provenance were not changed.

No actual CTest discovery/test, native suite, prerequisite/resource validation,
benchmark, pilot or GPU work ran. No fresh build, Release or ASan/UBSan run is
claimed. The new grammar intentionally rejects unsupported generated layouts;
boundary checks require an exclusively owned, quiescent tree and trusted tools.
Study launch remains **NO-GO** pending a separate independent review. This task
stops at the repair audit and does not authorize subsequent fresh validation.
